newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees 11.7 mln acres in Northern Plains in CRP.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees 11.7 mln acres in Northern Plains in CRP.

text.p: Agriculture Department chief economist Keith Collins said Wednesday that 11.7 million acres of cropland in the Northern Plains are estimated to be enrolled in the government's revamped Conservation Reserve Program, up 2.0 million acres from the current enrollment in that region.

He said a USDA analysis also shows that enrollment in the Southern Plains area will go down less than 500,000 acres from its current 5.3 million acre enrollment, and that Rocky Mountain states may see a one million acre decrease to 5.7 million acres.

Collins said that predicted enrollment is "essentially unchanged" in the Corn Belt, Delta and the Great Lakes states, slightly higher in the Northeast and slightly lower in the Southeast and the Pacific areas.
Collins cautioned, however, that current analysis is "very speculative."
USDA Wednesday announced new rules governing the Conservation Reserve Program for the next 10 years.

Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the first effect of the new rules will show up in winter wheat acreage this fall, and in 1998 corn and soybean acres. Glickman and Collins did not predict any major shift in crop acreage due to the new rules.
